stories.headline: Oil plunges 5% to three-week low as Qatar and Bessent signal a US-Iran deal on Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Front-month Brent futures fell $3.95, or 4.72%, to $79.82 a barrel on Aug. 4 after touching a session high of $86.33, while WTI fell $4.32, or 5.38%, to $76.02 — both the lowest since July 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Front-month Brent futures fell $3.95, or 4.72%, to $79.82 a barrel this afternoon after hitting a session high of $86.33. Prices fell to as low as $79.73 a barrel at one point, or down around 5%. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was down $4.32, or 5.38%, at $76.02 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday; Brent closed down 5.3% at $79.36 and WTI down 5.7% at $75.77.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices fell sharply Tuesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated there may be a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz as soon as this week. Brent, the international oil benchmark, slid 5.3% to close at $79.36 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate futures lost 5.7% to settle at $75.77.

key_facts.fact: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said diplomatic contacts had reached 'very progressive stages', with Qatar, Pakistan and Oman exchanging draft proposals between Washington and Tehran, while Iran denied any direct talks with the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said diplomatic contacts had reached 'very progressive stages.' He said mediators including Qatar, Pakistan and Oman were coordinating closely to facilitate negotiations and exchange draft proposals between Washington and Tehran.

key_facts.fact: Trump told Fox News the Strait of Hormuz would open 'very soon' or Iran would be 'hit very hard'; UK petrol prices have hit an average £1.60 a litre, back to levels seen at the start of the conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Donald Trump said the Strait of Hormuz would open 'very soon' or Iran would be 'hit very hard' as oil prices fell to a three-week low amid hopes of a deal. ... In the UK petrol prices are now at levels seen at the start of the conflict, with the average cost of a litre of petrol hitting £1.60, according to the RAC motoring group.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command confirmed on Aug. 4 that its forces have redirected 45 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two to enforce the blockade of Iranian ports reimposed on July 14.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed on August 4 that US forces have redirected 45 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two vessels to ensure compliance with its blockade on Iranian ports.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs expects Brent to stay in an $80-$90 range until either a new US-Iran agreement is confirmed or attacks escalate significantly.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs expects Brent to remain in an $80-$90 a barrel range until there is either confirmation of a new U.S.-Iran agreement or a significant escalation in attacks and targets.

stories.headline: US Army has used 'virtually all' its long-range precision missiles in the Iran war, sources say

key_facts.fact: Three people familiar with the data said the US Army has used up much of its stockpile of long-range precision missiles — principally ATACMS and the newer Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) — during the five-month war with Iran, with two saying 'virtually all' of these weapons have been expended.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during America's five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar with the data... The U.S. has used 'virtually all' of these weapons, according to two of the sources.

key_facts.fact: A CSIS report published last week estimated that about 65% of Patriot interceptors were expended between February and July, and that US THAAD interceptor stockpiles are at least 38% lower than at the start of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, CSIS published a report estimating that between February and July about 65% of Patriot interceptors had been expended and that the number of THAAD ballistic missile interceptors in U.S. stockpiles was at least 38% lower than at the start of the war.

key_facts.fact: The US has also burned through a little less than half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles since the war began, one source said; Raytheon has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon to boost Tomahawk production.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. also burned through a little less than half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles, which are generally launched from ships, since the start of the war, one of the sources said... Raytheon, a unit of RTX, has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon aimed at boosting Tomahawk production.

key_facts.fact: The supply figures circulated inside the federal government over the past week amid debate in the Trump administration over how much longer the US can keep striking Iran without limiting its ability to respond to crises elsewhere, including against Russia and China.
key_facts.excerpt: The supply figures have circulated inside the federal government over the last week during tense conversations inside the Trump administration about how much longer the U.S. can continue striking Iran without drawing down the stockpile to levels that would limit the military's ability to respond to crises elsewhere.

key_facts.fact: Trump launched the war jointly with Israel in February, predicting a short conflict; more than five months in, no request for a declaration of war or use-of-force authorization has been submitted to Congress.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time... No request for a declaration of war or an authorization to use military force has been submitted to Congress.

stories.headline: Novo Nordisk raises 2026 guidance on Wegovy pill but shares fall as the pill misses estimates

key_facts.fact: Novo Nordisk reported Q2 2026 net sales of DKK 78.49 billion (about $12.09 billion), up 3% at constant exchange rates, with adjusted sales up 7% and adjusted operating profit up 11% to DKK 33.39 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Q2 2026 reported sales increased by 3% at CER... Q2 2026 adjusted sales increased by 7% at CER, driven by GLP-1 volume growth across geographies... Q2 2026 adjusted operating profit increased by 11% at CER.

key_facts.fact: The company raised full-year 2026 guidance on Aug. 4 to adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit growth of 0% to -6% at constant exchange rates, up from -4% to -12% guided on May 6.
key_facts.excerpt: Bagsværd, Denmark, 4 August 2026 – Novo Nordisk today announced adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit for the second quarter of 2026 and raised 2026 full-year adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit outlook at CER... Adjusted sales growth 0% to -6% | -4% to -12%.

key_facts.fact: Oral Wegovy generated DKK 3.22 billion in the quarter, slightly below the DKK 3.27 billion analysts expected; US-traded shares fell about 6% on Tuesday and Copenhagen-listed shares fell about 5% on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Novo said its newly launched pill version of its Wegovy weight loss drug raked in 3.22 billion kroner for the second quarter. That's slightly below the 3.27 billion kroner that analysts were expecting... U.S.-traded shares of Novo Nordisk dropped about 6% on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The Wegovy pill has topped 5 million prescriptions since its January launch, with weekly US prescriptions above 265,000 in the week ending July 17; Novo says about 80% of pill patients had never used a GLP-1 before.
key_facts.excerpt: The pill has reached more than 5 million prescriptions since its launch... Novo said around 80% of patients taking the pill had not previously used a GLP-1 treatment, suggesting it is expanding the obesity market rather than simply drawing users away from injectable Wegovy.

key_facts.fact: Novo took DKK 6.3 billion in non-cash impairment charges on pipeline assets, including DKK 4.0 billion for monlunabant, the obesity candidate from its $1 billion 2023 Inversago acquisition, which it has now discontinued.
key_facts.excerpt: The pharma revealed that it had ended work on the oral cannabinoid receptor blocker monlunabant, which was in mid-stage development for obesity. The drug came from Novo's $1 billion acquisition of Inversago Pharma in August 2023.

key_facts.fact: CEO Mike Doustdar told reporters on Aug. 5 that 'we stay alive—or not—based on our ability to innovate', after the Phase 3 ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab in cardiovascular disease missed its primary endpoint.
key_facts.excerpt: "We stay alive—or not—based on our ability to innovate," Doustdar told reporters during a press call early Wednesday morning to present the Danish pharma's second quarter earnings results.

stories.headline: Saudi-led $55B buyout of Electronic Arts closes, the largest leveraged buyout on record

key_facts.fact: Electronic Arts announced on Aug. 4 that its acquisition by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners has closed; shareholders receive $210 in cash per share and EA's stock has ceased trading and will be delisted from Nasdaq.
key_facts.excerpt: REDWOOD CITY, Calif. – August 4, 2026 – Electronic Arts Inc. ... today announced that its acquisition by PIF, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners (collectively, the 'Consortium') has successfully closed... EA stockholders will receive $210 in cash for each share of EA common stock they owned as of the closing.

key_facts.fact: The deal is valued at $55bn and is thought to be the largest leveraged buyout ever, with PIF putting in $36bn and borrowing $20bn from JPMorgan, with the debt loaded onto the business.
key_facts.excerpt: It is thought to be the largest leveraged... as well as the $36bn it has already put into the deal, PIF needs to borrow $20bn from investment bankers JPMorgan to close it, with the business taking on the debt.

key_facts.fact: It ranks as the second-biggest acquisition in gaming history after Microsoft's $69bn purchase of Activision Blizzard; Affinity Partners is led by Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal ranks as the second-biggest acquisition in gaming history, after Microsoft's $69bn purchase of Activision Blizzard, the company behind Call of Duty. ... The investors, who include Affinity Partners - led by President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

key_facts.fact: The consortium's agreement was announced on September 29, 2025 and approved by EA shareholders on December 22, 2025; EA posted about $7.5 billion in GAAP net revenue in fiscal 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Consortium's agreement to acquire EA was previously announced on September 29, 2025, and was approved by EA stockholders at the special meeting of stockholders held on December 22, 2025... In fiscal year 2026, EA posted GAAP net revenue of approximately $7.5 billion.

stories.headline: India's central bank holds rates at 5.25% for a fourth meeting, lifts FY27 growth forecast to 6.7%

key_facts.fact: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on Aug. 5 to keep the repo rate at 5.25% and retain its neutral stance, the fourth consecutive meeting without a change.
key_facts.excerpt: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously voted to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and retain its neutral policy stance.

key_facts.fact: The RBI raised its FY27 real GDP growth projection to 6.7% from 6.6% and cut its CPI inflation forecast to 5.0% from 5.1%, with inflation seen peaking at 5.9% in the December quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday projected real GDP growth of 6.7% for 2026-27 and retail inflation at 5.0%, while warning that price pressures will peak at 5.9% in the December quarter before moderating... a slight upgrade from the RBI's June 2026 monetary policy assessment, which had pegged FY27 GDP growth at 6.6% and inflation at 5.1%.

key_facts.fact: Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the global environment had become increasingly unstable, citing the West Asia conflict disrupting trade routes and renewed escalation since early July that has driven volatility in energy prices.
key_facts.excerpt: He said the conflict in West Asia continued to disrupt... trade routes, while renewed escalation since early July had heightened volatility in global energy prices.

key_facts.fact: Headline retail inflation rose to 4.4% in June 2026, breaching the 4% target after 16 straight months below it, driven by food and fuel; core inflation excluding precious metals was just 2.3%-2.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: Headline retail inflation rose to 4.4% in June 2026, breaching the RBI's 4% target after remaining below it for 16 consecutive months... Excluding precious metals, however, core inflation stood at just 2.3%-2.5%.

key_facts.fact: The MPC flagged a deficient and uneven south-west monsoon amid El Niño as a key risk: as of Aug. 3 the cumulative monsoon deviation from normal was 11.9%, with 166 major reservoirs at 44.4% of capacity versus 69.3% a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: As of August 3, the cumulative monsoon deviation from normal stood at 11.9 per cent. Reservoir levels offered some comfort, with water storage across 166 major reservoirs at 44.4 per cent of capacity, though this was down from 69.3 per cent a year earlier.

stories.headline: A derelict Falcon 9 upper stage slams into the Moon as NASA tracks the impact live

key_facts.fact: NASA said on Aug. 4 that it and SpaceX were tracking a used Falcon 9 upper stage expected to impact the Moon on Wednesday, Aug. 5, near the Einstein and Bell craters, posing no danger to Earth.
key_facts.excerpt: Using ground-based telescopes and space-based assets, NASA and SpaceX are tracking a used Falcon 9 upper stage from a commercial mission expected to impact the Moon on Wednesday, Aug. 5, near the Einstein and Bell craters.

key_facts.fact: The stage came from the Jan. 15, 2025 Falcon 9 launch that deployed Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost 1 lander under NASA's CLPS initiative; solar activity and gravitational forces caused its unplanned return to the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: On Jan. 15, 2025, SpaceX launched the Falcon 9 rocket and successfully deployed Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost 1 lunar lander to the Moon under NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. Solar activity and gravitational forces caused the stage's unplanned return to the Moon.

key_facts.fact: Independent astronomers first spotted the trajectory using public data; NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies at JPL later confirmed a 100% chance of lunar impact.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent astronomers first identified the trajectory using publicly available data. NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California... later confirmed the stage has a 100% chance of impacting the Moon.

key_facts.fact: The stage is about the size of a five-storey building with a mass of at least 4,000 kg, travelling at roughly 2.43 km/s (about 5,400 mph); impact was predicted for about 02:35 EDT (06:35 GMT) on Aug. 5.
key_facts.excerpt: The piece in question is the upper stage of the rocket, and is about the size of a five-storey building, with a mass on Earth of at least 4,000kg (8,800 lbs). The impending collision - predicted to happen at about 02:35 EDT (06:35 GMT) on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The last derelict rocket to hit the Moon was a Chinese Long March 3C upper stage in 2022, from the 2014 Chang'e 5-T1 mission, which struck the far side.
key_facts.excerpt: The last dead rocket to impact the Moon was in 2022, when the Chinese Long March 3C upper stage from the 2014 Chang'e 5-T1 mission hit the far side of the Moon.

key_facts.fact: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and the ShadowCam instrument on South Korea's Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter will look for chances to image the site before and after impact.
key_facts.excerpt: Additionally, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and the ShadowCam instrument aboard South Korea's Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter will look for chances to image the site before and after the impact.

stories.headline: Ukraine's SBU says a 40-day campaign hit 100+ strategic targets in Russia, 14 of them refineries

key_facts.fact: In an Aug. 4 statement, Ukraine's Security Service said it struck more than 100 strategic military and industrial targets inside Russia and occupied territories during a 40-day campaign approved by President Zelenskyy.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says it has struck more than 100 strategic military and industrial targets inside Russia and occupied Ukrainian territories during a 40-day campaign approved by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. ... In a statement on 4 August, the SBU said the operation targeted Russia's military-industrial complex.

key_facts.fact: The SBU claimed strikes on the Saky, Hvardiiske, Belbek, Bagerovo, Engels and Khanskaya air bases, destroying one Tu-95MS strategic bomber and damaging two Su-35 fighters and two L-39 trainers.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency said it struck the Saky, Hvardiiske, Belbek, Bagerovo, Engels, and Khanskaya air bases, as well as the Yevpatoria aviation plant. It claimed the attacks destroyed one Tu-95MS strategic bomber, damaged two Su-35 fighter jets and two L-39 trainer aircraft.

key_facts.fact: It said it hit 14 oil refineries — naming St. Petersburg, Yaroslavl, Nizhny Novgorod, Perm, Volgograd and Ufa — plus dozens of oil depots and terminals, and four tankers tied to Russia's sanctions-evading 'shadow fleet'.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency said it also struck 14 oil refineries, dozens of oil depots, pumping stations, terminals, and storage facilities, naming refineries in St. Petersburg, Yaroslavl, Nizhny Novgorod, Perm, Volgograd, and Ufa among the targets. It further claimed attacks on the tankers Blue, Louise 1, Banda, and Avero.

key_facts.fact: Over the same 40 days, SBU frontline units claimed strikes on more than 21,000 pieces of Russian equipment and infrastructure and nearly 5,000 Russian troops killed, including 24 tanks, 124 artillery systems and 40 air defence systems.
key_facts.excerpt: the SBU said its frontline units struck more than 21,000 items of Russian military equipment, weapons, and infrastructure during the same 40-day period, while killing nearly 5,000 Russian troops... those strikes included 24 tanks, 63 armored vehicles, 124 artillery systems, 22 multiple-launch rocket systems, 40 air defense systems.

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 4 Ukraine's General Staff reported 216 combat clashes along the front, 23 of them on the Pokrovsk axis, with Russian forces deploying 6,428 kamikaze drones and dropping 213 guided aerial bombs in a single day.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces carried out 216 combat clashes across the front line as of 10 p.m. Tuesday, Aug. 4, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk axis... Russian forces also deployed 6,428 kamikaze drones.

key_facts.fact: Also on Aug. 4, Zelenskyy signed a decree sanctioning 23 companies and 20 individuals accused of supplying components to Russia's military-industrial complex, and named former defence minister Rustem Umerov head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a decree on imposing sanctions against companies and individuals accused of manufacturing and supplying components for Russia's military-industrial complex... The sanctions target 23 companies and 20 individuals... Zelenskyy said he had decided to appoint former Defense Minister... Rustem Umerov as head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service.
